skill.name: incremental-implementation
skill.description: Guides software work through small, complete increments that are tested, verified, and easy to review or revert. It helps teams manage multi-file features, refactors, feature flags, and large tasks.
skill.summary: A practical method for shipping tested, reviewable software increments.
skill.author: addyosmani

content.user_title: Build Software in Small, Verifiable Increments
content.value_statement: Large changes are difficult to test, review, and recover when problems appear late. This skill breaks work into complete increments with explicit tests, verification, and rollback points.
actual_capabilities: Breaks multi-file work into small vertical slices.
Defines contract-first and risk-first slicing strategies.
Requires testing and verification after each increment.
Recommends feature flags for incomplete functionality.
Promotes simple designs and focused scope.
Provides rollback-friendly commit and migration guidance.
limitations: It does not execute tests, builds, or commits.
It does not select repository-specific commands automatically.
It does not replace architecture, security, or code review.
It provides process guidance rather than project-specific implementation.

use_cases.title: Plan a Multi-File Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a large feature into complete vertical slices that can be tested and reviewed as they are built.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Frontend and Backend Work
use_cases.description: Use contract-first slicing to define shared interfaces before parallel implementation and integration.

use_cases.title: Reduce Delivery Risk
use_cases.description: Use risk-first slices, feature flags, and rollback-friendly changes when a task has uncertainty or incomplete functionality.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Small Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me split this change into the smallest complete increment. Identify the files, test, and verification step for the first increment.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Vertical Slices
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a vertical-slice plan for this feature. Each slice must deliver working behavior, include tests, and remain reviewable.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Contract First
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a contract-first sequence for this frontend and backend change. Separate the contract, backend, frontend, and integration checks.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Technical Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this implementation plan and reorder its increments by technical risk. Add feature flags, verification gates, and rollback points where needed.

output_examples.input: Add task creation, task listing, and task editing to an application.
output: Increment 1: create a task through the database, API, and basic interface.
Increment 2: list tasks through the query, API, and interface.
Increment 3: edit a task with focused tests and verification.

output_examples.input: Add a sharing feature that is not ready for all users.
output_examples.output: Add the sharing path behind a disabled-by-default feature flag. Test the flag-off behavior, then verify the enabled path before wider release.

output_examples.input: A new WebSocket integration has uncertain reliability.
output_examples.output: Start with a connection proof and its test. Add real-time updates only after the connection works, then add reconnection and offline behavior.

best_practices: Keep every increment complete, testable, and independently reviewable.
Address the riskiest or most uncertain technical assumption early.
Use explicit scope, verification gates, feature flags, and rollback points.
anti_patterns: Implementing an entire multi-file feature before testing.
Combining unrelated refactors, configuration changes, and features.
Adding abstractions or scope before a real use case requires them.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for multi-file features, refactors, feature flags, or tasks that feel too large to complete safely in one pass.

faq.question: What is a vertical slice?
faq.answer: A vertical slice is a small change that travels through the required layers and leaves working user-visible behavior.

faq.question: Should every increment be committed?
faq.answer: The skill recommends descriptive commits after verified increments so each change remains understandable and reversible.

faq.question: How does contract-first slicing help?
faq.answer: It gives parallel teams a shared interface before they implement separate backend and frontend pieces.

faq.question: When should I use a feature flag?
faq.answer: Use a flag when incomplete functionality must be merged without exposing it to users.

faq.question: Does this skill run project commands?
faq.answer: No. It recommends that the agent discover and run the repository's own tests, build, type-check, and lint commands.
